name: rule-guard
description: Enforces your rules on Bash commands in code, not by asking nicely: blocks AI attribution in commits and PRs, asks before destructive commands, and blocks patterns you choose, optionally only under certain folders.

blockAiAttribution.title: Block AI attribution
blockAiAttribution.description: Refuse git commit, gh pr and git tag commands whose text carries a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer or a 'Generated with Claude Code' footer. Claude is told to remove it and retry.

confirmDestructive.title: Ask before destructive commands
confirmDestructive.description: Ask you first before rm -rf on a broad target, git push --force, git reset --hard, git clean -f, DROP TABLE/DATABASE and chmod -R 777.

customDenyPattern.title: Block commands matching (regex)
customDenyPattern.description: A regular expression. A Bash command that matches is refused. Example: 9VP73Q9QX3 to keep one Apple team ID out of commands. Empty turns it off.

customDenyScope.title: Only when the session folder contains
customDenyScope.description: Comma-separated path fragments, such as /company/ or a project name. The custom pattern applies only when the session's folder path contains one of them. Empty means everywhere.

customDenyMessage.title: Message for the custom block
customDenyMessage.description: What Claude is told when the custom pattern blocks a command.
customDenyMessage.default: This command matches a pattern you blocked.
